_note: Summaries for books the StoryGraph scrape could not resolve. Written by hand from reference sources rather than copied from publisher copy, and kept here so a rebuild cannot lose them. sgmerge.py folds these in after sg_desc.jsonl, and only where a book has no summary already — so if StoryGraph later resolves one of these, the scraped text still does not overwrite what is here. Key is the books.json title.
Night of Knives: Malaz Island is a backwater now, for all that it gave the empire its name. For one night it is not: a Shadow Moon has come, the once-a-generation convergence that opens the way for demon hounds and older things, and the same night is prophesied to bring the return of the vanished Emperor Kellanved. Everyone with a reason to stop that gathers on the island at once. A single night, told from street level by two people who did not choose to be in the middle of it. Set around the events behind the prologue of Gardens of the Moon.
Opening Atlantis: Three linked novellas on an Earth with an eighth continent sitting in the Atlantic between Europe and North America. An English fisherman, sick of political repression at home, settles it in 1452 and finds he has brought his troubles with him — an exiled noble means to rule the place. His descendants put down the pirate havens of Avalon generations later, and are drawn into the Anglo-French wars of the eighteenth century. A family and a continent over three hundred years, rather than a single plot.
The Jennifer Morgue: Second of the Laundry Files. Bob Howard is pointed at a billionaire trying to raise a sunken Soviet submarine and the occult device aboard it that lets you interrogate the dead — a second run at what the CIA botched with the Glomar Explorer in 1975, and one that risks waking something that stopped the first attempt. The target has warded his island so that only people who fit spy-thriller stereotypes can make landfall, which obliges Bob to play Bond. Expense receipts are still required, and the auditors are worse than the Great Old Ones.
Mélusine: First of the Doctrine of Labyrinths. Felix Harrowgate is a wizard who has buried a baseborn past under a court title, until his former master breaks his mind and uses him to shatter the working that holds the city's magic together. Mildmay is a cat burglar, trained young as an assassin, who gets caught by a charm meant for Felix. The two are bound together and driven out of Melusine, narrated in alternating first person by a man who cannot trust his own senses and one who will not talk about himself.
The Curse of the Mistwraith: Two half-brothers, the sunlit prince Lysaer and the shadow-wielding bastard Arithon, are exiled through a gate into Athera, a world where a curse of mist has blotted out the sun for five centuries. Only their combined gifts can lift it, and the Mistwraith, as it dies, binds the pair into a geas of mutual hatred that turns the rescue of a world into the opening move of a war between them. Dense, slow and ornately written, the first volume of Janny Wurts's eleven-book Wars of Light and Shadow.
She Is the Darkness: The Black Company, now in Shadowmaster country under Lady's command, lays siege to Overlook and Longshadow's ally Soulcatcher while Croaker, Lady, Murgen and the Nyueng Bao work out who is betraying whom. Murgen's Annals close the Glittering Stone sequence's first half on the plain of shining stone, where the Company's oldest secret waits. Seventh of the Black Company novels.
Towers of Midnight: The penultimate Wheel of Time novel. Perrin faces the Whitecloaks and his own wolf nature, Mat enters the Tower of Ghenjei to free Moiraine, Egwene holds the reunited White Tower against the Black Ajah, and Rand, now at peace with himself, prepares the nations for the Last Battle while the Seals on the Dark One's prison weaken.
The Sword and the Chain: Karl Cullinane and the surviving college friends are trapped in the fantasy world their game brought them to, and Karl has sworn to end slavery there. The second Guardians of the Flame novel follows the founding of Home, a free settlement in the wilds, the raids that fund it, and the price of trying to build something just in a world that runs on chains.
The Plague of Swords: Fourth of the Traitor Son Cycle. With the Wild's great alliance broken, Gabriel Muriens, the Red Knight, turns to the dragon Ash and the sorcerer-priest Master Smythe, whose plague of swords is a weapon aimed at the whole world. Armies converge on Alba and Galle, the Emperor's court plays its own game, and Gabriel has to decide how much of the world he is willing to spend to save the rest of it.
